entities.name: Machu Picchu
entities.label: Place
entities.summary: A 15th-century Inca citadel perched at 2,430m in the Peruvian Andes, built for Emperor Pachacuti (c. 1450). Its precision dry-stone masonry, agricultural terraces, and astronomical alignments demonstrate extraordinary Inca engineering. Abandoned during the Spanish conquest and revealed to the outside world by Hiram Bingham in 1911, it is now a UNESCO World Heritage Site and symbol of pre-Columbian achievement.
